items.title: 7.1.7 Motion of a Free Particle Moving Along a Vertical Line (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 229: 7.1.7 free vertical motion, g = 9.8 m/s^2, replace a by g (down) or -g (up); Example 11 Free Fall from Rest and Example 12 Upward Throw

blocks.text: Bachon, aaj ka sabaq hamari rozmarra zindagi se juda hai. Aap ne dekha hoga ke chhat se koi cheez girti hai to har lamhe tez hoti jati hai, aur jab aap gaind ko seedha oopar uchhaalte hain to woh dheemi hoti hoti ek pal ruk jati hai aur phir wapas aati hai. Dono kaamon ke peeche ek hi cheez hai: gravity (zameen ki kashish). Achhi khabar yeh hai ke is ke liye koi nayi equation nahin chahiye. 7.1.6 wali teen equations hi kaam karengi, bas acceleration \(a\) ki jagah \(g\) ya \(-g\) rakhna hoga. Aaj hum seekhenge ke kab \(+g\) aur kab \(-g\), aur do kitabi misaalein hal karenge.

Kitab kehti hai: jab koi particle sirf gravity ke asar mein chale aur hawa ki rukawat (air resistance) ko nazarandaz kar diya jaye, to is motion ko free fall ya free vertical motion kehte hain. Yeh motion ek khari seedhi line mein hoti hai, ya oopar ki taraf ya neeche ki taraf. Gravity ki wajah se acceleration ko \(g\) se zahir karte hain, aur yeh taqreeban itna hai:

blocks.text_alt: g equals 9.8 metres per second squared

blocks.text: Agar particle ko oopar phenka jaye to gravity ki wajah se us ki velocity yaksaan tareeqe se kam hoti jati hai aur sab se oonche point par zero ho jati hai. Agar particle neeche ki taraf chal raha ho to woh zameen ki taraf \(g\) ki sharah se tez hota jata hai. Constant acceleration wali equations of motion vertical motion mein bhi use ho sakti hain: neeche ki motion ke liye \(a\) ki jagah \(g\), aur oopar ki motion ke liye \(-g\) rakhein.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\) ka matlab kya hai? Girti hui cheez ki velocity har second mein 9.8 m/s barh jati hai: 1 second baad 9.8, 2 second baad 19.6, 3 second baad 29.4 m/s. Yeh value cheez ke wazan par munhasir nahin: hawa na ho to pathar aur pankh ek saath girte hain.
Ab sign ka masla. Hum hamesha motion ki simt ko positive maante hain. Neeche girti cheez ke liye neeche positive hai aur gravity bhi neeche khinchti hai, is liye \(a = +g\): raftaar barhti hai. Oopar jaati cheez ke liye oopar positive hai lekin gravity neeche khinchti hai, yani motion ke ulat, is liye \(a = -g\): raftaar ghat-ti hai. Neeche ki table dono haalaton ki equations saath saath dikhati hai.

blocks.caption: Gravity ke saath equations of motion, \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\) (hamari taraf se; positive simt = motion ki simt)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Oopar phenki gayi gaind sab se oonche point par ek pal ke liye ruk jati hai. Us lamhe us ki velocity kya hai, aur acceleration kya hai?
Jawab: velocity zero hai (\(v = 0\)), lekin acceleration zero nahin! Gravity us waqt bhi \(9.8\) m/s\(^2\) neeche khinch rahi hai, isi liye gaind wahan ruki nahin rehti balke wapas girne lagti hai. Yeh exam ka pasandeeda sawal hai.

blocks.title: Example 11
blocks.problem: (Free Fall from Rest) A stone is dropped from the top of a tower 45 m high. Find the time taken to reach the ground and the final velocity on impact.
steps:
Diya gaya: pathar chhoda gaya hai (phenka nahin), is liye \(u = 0\); minar ki oonchai \(x = 45\) m; motion neeche ki taraf hai, is liye \(a = g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
Maloom karna: zameen tak pohanchne ka waqt \(t\) aur takraate waqt velocity \(v\).
Tareeqa: \(u\), \(x\), \(a\) maloom hain aur \(t\) chahiye; \(v\) na diya hai na pehle hisse mein poocha, is liye \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^{2}\) lein. Phir \(t\) mil jaye to \(v = u + gt\).

Equation of motion use karein
\[x = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}\]
Values rakhein:
\[45 = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}(9.8)t^{2}\]
\[45 = 4.9\,t^{2}\]
Kyun: "dropped" ka matlab hai haath se chhod diya, koi dhakka nahin diya, is liye shuru ki velocity zero hai aur \(ut\) wala term khatam ho gaya.

\(t\) ke liye hal karein
\[t = \sqrt{\dfrac{45 \times 2}{9.8}}\]
\[= \sqrt{9.18} \approx 3.03 \text{ s}\]
Kyun: dono taraf 4.9 se taqseem kiya aur square root liya. Waqt negative nahin ho sakta, is liye sirf positive root liya.
Dhyan dein: \(\sqrt{\frac{90}{9.8}}\) ki jagah \(\frac{90}{9.8}\) par ruk jana aam ghalti hai; woh \(t^{2}\) hai, \(t\) nahin.

Takraate waqt velocity
\[v = u + gt\]
\[v = 0 + 9.8 \times 3.03\]
\[\approx 29.7 \text{ m/s}\]
Kyun: har second velocity 9.8 m/s barhti hai, aur pathar taqreeban 3.03 second girta hai.

Tasdeeq:
Teesri equation se, jis mein \(t\) ki zaroorat hi nahin:
\[v^{2} = u^{2} + 2gx = 0 + 2 \times 9.8 \times 45 = 882\]
\[v = \sqrt{882} \approx 29.7 \text{ m/s}\]
Wahi jawab. Yeh tareeqa round kiye hue \(t\) par munhasir nahin, is liye zyada pakka hai.
blocks.answer: Time \(t \approx 3.03\) s; final velocity on impact \(v \approx 29.7\) m/s (downward).

blocks.title: Example 12
blocks.problem: (Upward Throw) A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. Find, the maximum height attained and the time to reach the maximum height.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(u = 20\) m/s (oopar ki taraf), sab se oonche point par \(v = 0\) m/s, aur motion oopar ki taraf hai is liye \(a = -g = -9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
Maloom karna: zyada se zyada oonchai, aur us oonchai tak pohanchne ka waqt.
Tareeqa: chhupi hui value pehchaaniye: choti par gaind ek pal ruk jati hai, yani \(v = 0\). Pehle \(v = u + at\) se waqt, phir \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2}\) se oonchai.

Choti tak pohanchne ka waqt
\[v = u + gt \quad (g \text{ ki jagah } -9.8)\]
\[0 = 20 + (-9.8)t\]
\[9.8\,t = 20\]
\[t = \dfrac{20}{9.8} \approx 2.04 \text{ s}\]
Kyun: gaind har second 9.8 m/s raftaar khoti hai; 20 m/s khone mein \(\frac{20}{9.8}\) second lagenge. Yahan \(g\) ki jagah \(-9.8\) is liye rakha kyun ke gravity motion ke ulat hai (kitab isi ko \(g = -9.8\) likhti hai; dekhiye neeche "Kitab ki ghalti").

Zyada se zyada oonchai
\[x = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2} \quad (g \text{ ki jagah } -9.8)\]
\[x = 20 \times 2.04 + \dfrac{1}{2}(-9.8)(2.04)^{2}\]
\[= 40.8 - 20.39\]
\[\approx 20.4 \text{ m}\]
Kyun: pehla term woh faasla hai jo gaind bina gravity ke tay karti; doosra (minus wala) term gravity ki wajah se kam hone wala faasla hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{1}{2}(-9.8)\) ka minus bhool jayein to \(61.2\) m jaisa ghalat jawab aata hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(t\) ke baghair wali equation:
\[2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\]
\[2(-9.8)x = 0 - 400\]
\[x = \dfrac{400}{19.6} \approx 20.4 \text{ m}\]
Wahi jawab. Is ke ilawa, yaad rakhiye ke gaind ko wapas aane mein bhi itna hi waqt (2.04 s) lagta hai, yani kul 4.08 s hawa mein rehti hai.
blocks.answer: Time to reach the maximum height \(t \approx 2.04\) s; maximum height \(\approx 20.4\) m.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
1. Sawal mein "Find, the maximum height" chhapa hai; comma faltu hai: "Find the maximum height".
2. Hal mein kitab \(a = g = -9.8\) m/s\(^2\) likhti hai aur phir \(v = u + gt\) aur \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^{2}\) lagati hai. Lekin kitab ne abhi \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\) (positive) bataya tha aur kaha tha ke oopar ki motion mein \(a\) ki jagah \(-g\) likho. Sahi aur ek jaisa tareeqa: \(a = -g = -9.8\) m/s\(^2\), yani \(v = u - gt\) aur \(x = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^{2}\). Rakhi gayi values (\(-9.8\)) wahi hain, is liye jawab 2.04 s aur 20.4 m bilkul sahi hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh misaalein hamari taraf se hain.)
1. Ek pathar 20 m oonchi chhat se chhoda jata hai. Zameen tak kitna waqt?
\[20 = \tfrac{1}{2}(9.8)t^{2} \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{\tfrac{40}{9.8}} \approx 2.02 \text{ s}\]
Velocity: \(v = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 20} = \sqrt{392} \approx 19.8\) m/s.
2. Ek gaind 9.8 m/s se seedhi oopar phenki jati hai. Choti tak waqt \(t = \frac{9.8}{9.8} = 1\) s, aur oonchai \(x = 9.8 \times 1 - 4.9 \times 1 = 4.9\) m.
Ghor kijiye: doosri misaal mein velocity aadhi karne se oonchai chauthai ho jati hai (Example 12 ki 20 m/s se 20.4 m), kyun ke oonchai \(\frac{u^{2}}{2g}\) hai, yani velocity ke square ke hisaab se.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Free fall: sirf gravity ka asar, hawa ki rukawat nahin; \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
2. Neeche ki motion mein \(a = g\), oopar ki motion mein \(a = -g\); equations wahi teen.
3. "Dropped" ya "falls from rest" ka matlab \(u = 0\).
4. Sab se oonche point par \(v = 0\), lekin acceleration phir bhi \(g\) neeche ki taraf hai.
5. Choti tak waqt \(t = \frac{u}{g}\), zyada se zyada oonchai \(\frac{u^{2}}{2g}\).
6. Jawab ko hamesha doosri equation se tasdeeq karein (\(2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\) waqt ke baghair kaam karti hai).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Oopar ki motion mein \(g\) ka minus bhool jana; is se oonchai bohat zyada aa jati hai.
2. Sab se oonche point par acceleration ko bhi zero samajhna.
3. \(t^{2}\) nikaal kar square root lena bhool jana.
4. Chhode gaye pathar mein \(u\) ko 9.8 ya koi aur value de dena; chhode jane par \(u = 0\) hai.
5. Ek hi sawal mein ek jagah \(g = 9.8\) aur doosri jagah \(g = -9.8\) likhna; behtar hai \(g = 9.8\) rakhein aur sign equation mein lagayein.
